answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because lagoon only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any ripple approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
